reviews.title: Complete Trash at first
reviews.comment: This CPU was a waste of money at the time when I first purchased it.  I spent so much money upgrading from socket AM3+ to AM4 that I lost count of how much money I spent only to discover that every operating system that I have will not run with this CPU.  Noting I currently have is compatible with it except maybe DOS which is  pretty much completely useless today. It seems that it's only compatible with Mac-Row Soft windows HO-HO and Windows Ding-Dong.  Or in other words, It was designed to just run a gaming operating system and that's about it.  This will be the last AMD system that I will build due to all the headaches and problems that I went through to get it installed and running on a ASUS Prime X370A motherboard from 2017. I had to do some extensive research and purchase 2 addition CPU's (A6-9500 and Ryzen 5 3600)  to make sure this old mother board actually worked (which surprisingly it did) and to get the BIOS updated to the lastest 2024 BIOS to support this Ryzen 7 5700 CPU which I finally achieved today.  I currently have Fedora 33 Linux installed and working fine. Next I will have to download modified drivers for Windows 2000,  XP 64 bit and Vista 64 Bit and install those too. I don't run any newer Microsoft Operating System because of how wide the tool chains are and how dangerous they are to have connected to the internet.  I learnt the hard way to never trust Microsoft security updates again because they don't work.
reviews.author: Harry E. Cassidy

reviews.title: Cooler Came Jacked Up, Processor is a Beast
reviews.comment: Replaced an i5-8400 with this guy. Was good for the price, but I had to replace the cooler. On paper, this thing is supposed to handle things just fine (TDP for TDP). In reality...different story. I was monitoring system temps while performing basic tasks and they were always abnormally high (50C idle, 70C at 40% load). This was with the stock thermal paste. I ended up having to take my rig back apart and inspected the surfaces for both my CPU and the cooler. CPU was smooth as butter. Cooler? Not so much. Saw a few gouges and a couple small pieces of metal in the compound. Hoping that I could compensate with a good thermal paste and verifying good application, I saw absolutely no change in temperatures. Sadly, the cooler comes bundled with the processor so best I can hope for is the AMD RMA process, which nobody has time for. Conclusion? Just get your own cooler, even if you get this processor. Hopefully mine was just messed up at the factory, but it wasn't cutting the mustard on light tasks, which means it would have been hurting under heavy load. Thankfully, there is more than just the cooler in this package. The processor itself is, to put it lightly, in a different league than the 8400. Cold boot? 6 seconds. Shutting down? 2.5 seconds. Windows 10 installs faster than you can blink. It's more than sufficiently fast for my needs so far, especially coming from the experience I had with the 8400. Apparently there's controversy around the 5700 being a 5700g with the APU disabled. Coming in from being an Intel guy for so long, I really have no basis for comparison. I ended up with a bunch more cores, threads, fabrics, rebars, gidgets, and gadgets than I had before. For the price I paid, even with having to get another cooler, it's worth it. Would I have enjoyed a frustration-free experience for a few extra bucks? Heck yeah. That cooler was polished with a brillo pad and it almost makes me wonder if I was working with a refurb in disguise, but I digress. Still worth it. Now happy to be on team red.
reviews.author: neo_styles
